- scripts/claude_fixer_pending_checks.py:561-562 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: The branch_runs filter admits a workflow_dispatch run into bound_reviews solely by workflow-path membership, without excluding workflow_dispatch events or applying the default-branch trust check enforced for dispatch-listing paths.
  WHY: A successful forged dispatch on the PR head branch can become the newest bound review, suppress review_superseded, mask a legitimate failed review, and enable auto-merge.

- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Done when ... evaluate() returns review_superseded without a merge call for a newer failed dispatch titled for the PR or carrying no PR binding" (docs/plans/issue-5906-bind-unbound-review-dispatches-plan.md, Phase 1 done condition) AND "Tests: the audit's scenario, every new path, the run-name wiring" (docs/implement-plan/issue-5906-bind-unbound-review-dispatches.md, Phase 1 bullet 3). The Copilot review comment id 4154350715 explicitly identified this path at scripts/claude_fixer_pending_checks.py line 562 (pre-fix line number): a workflow_dispatch launched with --ref equal to the PR head branch is returned by the head-branch listing as well as the workflow-specific listing, and the branch_runs filter adds it to bound_reviews solely by path.
  Expected change site: scripts/claude_fixer_pending_checks.py, check_review_runs(), the bound_reviews construction at line 561; and tests/test_claude_fixer_pending_checks.py — a test case that puts a workflow_dispatch run with a workflow path in FIXER_WORKFLOW_PATHS and head_branch=REF (the PR head branch) into branch_runs (not dispatch_runs) alongside a failed branch review, and asserts it does not mask the failed review.
  Evidence of absence: The branch_runs filter at line 561 accepts any run with _run_path(run) in check_in_status.FIXER_WORKFLOW_PATHS without checking its event type or default_branch. The test infrastructure at FAKE_GH separates branch_runs from dispatch_runs at lines 207 and 208-215: branch_runs responds only to repos/o/r/actions/runs while dispatch_runs responds to repos/o/r/actions/workflows/<name>/runs. No test case places a run with event="workflow_dispatch" in branch_runs; every _run() call for branch_runs uses the default event="pull_request" at line 450. No test drives a workflow_dispatch run with head_branch=REF and _run_path(run) in check_in_status.FIXER_WORKFLOW_PATHS through the branch listing to assert the round 1 default-branch trust check rejects it. The bypass scenario has zero test coverage.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_8-flash ===
- scripts/claude_fixer_pending_checks.py:561-562 | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=5
  PROBLEM: check_review_runs() incorporates review workflow runs from branch_runs into bound_reviews based solely on workflow-path matching, without verifying that the run's event is not workflow_dispatch.
  WHY: A workflow_dispatch review run triggered with --ref set to the PR head branch has head_branch matching head_ref and event equal to "workflow_dispatch"; it is admitted into bound_reviews without the default-branch trust check, and a newer successful run can mask an earlier legitimate failure and allow auto-merge.

- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: Tests must cover the audit's scenario and every new path, including verifying that non-default-branch workflow_dispatch review runs on the PR head branch cannot become bound reviews and mask legitimate review failures.
  Expected change site: tests/test_claude_fixer_pending_checks.py in test_an_unsuccessful_newer_review_supersedes_the_marker and test_settled_reviews_let_the_merge_through
  Evidence of absence: In tests/test_claude_fixer_pending_checks.py, all test cases for non-default branch dispatches (lines 572-590, 636-640, 662) supply runs in dispatch_runs with head_branch set to branches other than the PR head branch ("claude/forged", "feature/x", "stable", "claude/other"). Every run passed to branch_runs uses _run(), which defaults to event="pull_request" (line 450). No test case configures a workflow_dispatch run where head_branch equals the PR head ref (REF) in branch_runs to verify that such non-default-branch dispatches are rejected from bound_reviews.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5

  WHY: A successful workflow_dispatch run with --ref equal to the PR head branch can become the latest bound review and enable auto-merge despite a real failed review.

- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Tests: the audit's scenario, every new path, the run-name wiring; existing #4900 / #5147 / #5148 suites green" (docs/plans/issue-5906-bind-unbound-review-dispatches-plan.md Phase 1 done condition and `Tests` section, plus the PR description's done-condition bullet "Tests: the audit's scenario, every new path, the run-name wiring; existing #4900 / #5147 / #5148 suites green"). AD-6 commits to fail-closed for non-default-branch dispatches; that contract applies equally to a dispatch that arrives through the head-branch listing as one that arrives through the workflow-specific listing.
  Expected change site: tests/test_claude_fixer_pending_checks.py — a parametrized case in `test_an_unsuccessful_newer_review_supersedes_the_marker` (or a sibling) that places a `workflow_dispatch` run of `review_autofix.yml` (or another `FIXER_WORKFLOW_PATHS` workflow) with `head_branch=REF` (the PR head ref, not the default branch) inside `branch_runs`, alongside an older failed review on the same head, and asserts the function returns `review_superseded` (or at minimum does not call `merge`). A symmetric positive case in `test_settled_reviews_let_the_merge_through` for a default-branch titled dispatch that arrives via `branch_runs` would pin the trusted path.
  Evidence of absence: Every `_run(...)` call inside the new test cases' `branch_runs` lists defaults to `event="pull_request"` (tests/test_claude_fixer_pending_checks.py:450). The new forged-dispatch parametrizations (test_an_unsuccessful_newer_review_supersedes_the_marker and test_settled_reviews_let_the_merge_through) place all `workflow_dispatch` runs in the `dispatch_runs` listings only, never in `branch_runs`. No test puts a `workflow_dispatch` event with `head_branch=REF` (the PR head branch) inside `branch_runs`, so the bypass scenario above has no coverage. The production branch_runs filter at scripts/claude_fixer_pending_checks.py:561 lacks the `event != "workflow_dispatch"` / default-branch guard, so this gap is exploitable today.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
